body:
Working entry: «Budget gate removed — no rate-limits reading, `budget.json`, send gate, `budget-paused`, budget board or
log fields, Path 6 suite; driver `release` guard kept; exit 11 retired» (viola-0.2.0, Epoch 2 — The budget gate and the
status line leave; id chk-vr5sssyv). The entry carries no freight (the `pins` view holds no block for chk-vr5sssyv).

Remove the budget gate whole, on the founder's ruling «Убрать совсем» (2026-11-08, `viola-0.2.0-incubator/intent.md`
§i): viola reads no rate limits and gates nothing on budget; the budget is the founder's own instrument. This is a
REMOVAL chunk: every surface of the gate leaves the product and its tests; the driver `release` guard stays; exit code 11
is retired and never renumbered or reused. The status-line interception itself (the pass-through to the user's command)
is the next entry's («Status-line interception removed»), not this one's.

The phase directive's seven items are the operator's directive for this chunk (inputs#I1; source:
`~/dev/projects/additional/viola-overseer/phase-budget-gate-removed-directive.md`): scope is the route entry as it
stands, a REMOVAL — every surface that leaves (code, tests, fixtures, schemas, docs, masters' rows) and everything that
stays, with why, named here; a thing the entry does not name that would leave with it is a fork on the card, never a
silent cut. The pinned product binary driving this session and the live home `~/.viola/` are not touched — no install,
no re-pin, no write under `~/.viola/`; a step needing one is a named operator step that waits. No live `claude` start
without a per-chunk cap (a named operator step that waits), no live desktop step; a print-and-exit `claude --version` is
no live start. No mutation run, local or dispatched: a guard test's one-off remove-the-guard control goes through
`gate.py control` under a kill deadline, its `case` the test's NAME alone, its entry reaching the case past fail-fast,
«holds» = that case ran and FAILED. Every statement in the plan about how a tool, a crate or the CLI behaves is measured
at P3 and cited, or marked unmeasurable. A red or defect found now folds into this chunk as an `[inferred]` item with
its own acceptance; one found at P3 outside the pinned scope is a Carry-forward naming its owner entry. The phase runs
exactly as the letters say, the operator away (his forks to the away form's file), and the P5 card carries the
directive's item-7 block.

body:
# Phase directive — «Budget gate removed» (Epoch 2, viola-0.2.0)

1. Scope is the route entry as it stands: no rate-limits reading, no `budget.json`, no send gate, no `budget-paused`,
   no budget board or log fields, no Path 6 suite; the driver `release` guard KEPT; exit 11 retired. It is a REMOVAL:
   name at P1 every surface that leaves (code, tests, fixtures, schemas, docs, masters' rows) and everything that
   stays and why; a thing the entry does not name that would leave with it is a fork on the card, not a silent cut.
2. The PINNED product binary that drives this very session (`~/.local/viola-product/bin/viola`,
   `~/.viola/bin/0.1.0-…`) and the live home `~/.viola/` are NOT touched by this chunk: no install, no re-pin, no write
   under `~/.viola/`. A step that would need one is a NAMED operator step that waits.
3. No live `claude` start is planned without a per-chunk cap; if the plan needs one it is a NAMED operator step that
   waits. No live desktop step. A print-and-exit read (`claude --version`) is no live start.
4. No mutation run, local or dispatched. A guard test carries its one-off remove-the-guard control through
   `gate.py control`, under a kill deadline; the control's `case` is the test's NAME alone, its entry reaches the case
   past fail-fast, and the controls file stands where implement's letter puts it. «Holds» = that case ran and FAILED.
5. Before any statement in the plan about how a tool, a crate or the CLI BEHAVES, measure it at P3 and cite the
   measurement; a statement that cannot be measured at plan time is marked as such.
6. A red or a defect found now folds into THIS chunk as an `[inferred]` item with its own acceptance; one found at P3
   outside the pinned scope is a Carry-forward naming its owner entry.
7. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. The operator is away: a fork that is his goes to the away form's file
   and the phase stops there. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the union's
   `picked {n} of {N}` per master with «by every draw» and the `rows-union` line; whether EVERY row the plan cites is
   in the union or its `*-standing.md` (name each in neither); every `[RETYPED]` line and `[EVERY_ROW]` re-spawn;
   every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` / `INDETERMINATE` / `NOT DERIVED` line, and every place a letter was wrong
   or silent. A plan that needs a new KEY of a master's keyed section, or to clear a NOT YET MEASURED piece of a mark,
   says so on the card.

body: - A `config.json` still carrying `five_hour` / `seven_day` after the removal is read by no threshold reader; the process's diagnostics-level read counts each as an unknown key and logs one `parse-rejected{parser:"config-json", detail:"unknown-keys", count:N}` WARN line at its start (`src/obs.rs:207-215` with the shrunk `CONFIG_KEYS`); `read_hold` ignores them (`src/run/dialog.rs:177`). - A NEW snapshot lacking `budget_paused` fails to parse in an OLD (0.1.0) reader, whose `budget_paused: bool` is required (`snapshot.rs:49`): an old binary then replays it, gets no endpoint, and its frame verbs read the instance unreachable. Mixed-binary reads across the upgrade are therefore one-way.

- A stamp still holding `statusline-rate-limits` (`pass` or `fail`) is read only on the 23 relied rows (`ledger.rs:1241`): a version stamped `23 pass  1 fail` with the failing row the rate-limits one reads verified after the removal.

- Does removing `budget_paused` from the snapshot, the `budget` param from `release` params and the `budget` / `budget_paused` fields from the `list` payload bump `v`, per `decision/protocol-version-bump-rule` («removing a field … bumps `v`»; `contract/protocol-version/v`: every channel `params`, event line and snapshot)? → blocks: plan-decision
- What does a new wrapper answer to a `release` carrying a `budget` key (skipped as an unknown field, or `-32602` `invalid-params` after the string-`from` check)? → blocks: plan-decision

title: I2-founder-forks.md.txt
body:
# Founder forks — 2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed (phase P4, the away form)

The phase stopped at P4 on the one fork below; nothing is planned past it. The promotion stands (`route.py promote`,
tx 1157), the row read and the research are done (`doc:2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed/research`), and the scope is at
rev 2. Answer here, or in a message; the phase resumes at P4 on the answer.

## Q1 — Does the removal bump `v`?

**What forces the question.** `architecture · decision/protocol-version-bump-rule`: «Adding a field or event kind is
additive and needs no bump of `v`; removing a field or changing its meaning bumps `v`.»
`architecture · contract/protocol-version/v`: `v` is carried in every channel `params`, ndjson event line and snapshot.
This chunk removes fields from all three surfaces' contracts: the snapshot loses `budget_paused` and
`budget_override_until`; the channel `release` loses its `budget` param and its reply's `budget_paused` /
`override_until`; the `list` payload (CLI `--json` and MCP `list`) loses `budget` and each item's `budget_paused`; the
event kind `budget-gate` is no longer written.

**Measured at P3** (`doc:2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed/research`, «Measured facts»):
- A new reader reads an old snapshot and an old log: the budget fields are skipped, an old `budget-gate` line is counted
  in `skipped.unknown_kinds` (`crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs:37`; the events reader).
- An OLD (0.1.0) reader cannot parse a new snapshot: its `budget_paused` is a required field (`snapshot.rs:49`), so it
  replays the log, gets no endpoint and reads the instance unreachable — it writes no frame (fails closed).
- A bump of the snapshot's `v` gives an old reader the same outcome by another route (unsupported `v` → replay).
- A bump of the channel's `v` makes every call between an old client and a new wrapper, either way, `-32602`
  `unsupported protocol version` until both sides are upgraded.

**Options, in order (recommendation first):**

1. **Keep every `v` at 1 (Recommended).** The fields leave on your ruling «Убрать совсем» (2026-11-08); the wrap
   amends `decision/protocol-version-bump-rule` with an exception naming this retirement. Why it wins: an old reader
   already fails closed on a new snapshot (no frame, no command run), a new reader reads every old file, and nothing
   else in the fleet changes; the upgrade is one `cargo install`, after which a session started under the old binary is
   restarted to be reached by the new CLI. Trade-off: the written rule gets an exception; a mixed fleet during the
   upgrade reads new instances as unreachable from an old CLI.
2. **Bump the snapshot's `v` to 2 only; the channel and the documents stay at 1.** New readers accept 1 and 2. Why
   not first: old readers end where option 1 leaves them (replay, unreachable), so the bump adds a reader branch and a
   `snapshot-unsupported-v` line in old logs for no change of outcome; the channel and `list` removals still need the
   rule's exception.
3. **Bump every `v` the rule names to 2 (snapshot, channel `params`, event line).** Follows the rule as written. Trade-off:
   during the upgrade every old-client/new-wrapper call is refused both ways, the live fleet's CLI and wrapped sessions
   must all move together, and the event line's `v` changes though no event field is removed (only a kind stops being
   written, which the rule calls additive in the other direction).

## Leans the plan will take without asking (shown here so the answer can overrule any of them)

- **The `statusline-rate-limits` ledger row leaves in this chunk** (relied 24 → 23): leaned per v2-04's own
  requirement («no `statusline-rate-limits` ledger row») and the census rows routed to v2-04 (C-205, C-286, C-587,
  C-747).
- **A new wrapper refuses a `release` carrying any `budget` key** with `-32602` `invalid-params` (`data: null`), after
  the string-`from` check, which stays first: leaned per the invariant «the human always wins» — an old
  `viola release --budget` meant «leave the wheel», and a wrapper that skipped the key would hand a human-held wheel
  to the driver — and because skipping it would admit an input the wrapper refuses today (the playbook's «Boundary
  widening» pattern, `rul-r74hshif`).
- **The board's WHEEL column stays 23 characters** wide: leaned per your confirmation of WHEEL 23 as your wording
  (2026-10-13) and the board width you ratified (2026-10-20); narrowing it to `unknown` (7) would move every row's bytes
  and the 65-column NAME cap. The row's stated reason («the width of its widest word») is re-worded at wrap.
- **The BAY line keeps only its non-budget cells**: `BAY  skipped a - b - c`, the four budget cells leaving per the
  entry («no … budget board … fields»).
- **`fixtures/claude/2.1.302/Mcp.tools-list-1.json` stays as recorded**: its replay reads no description; a re-record
  needs a live `claude` start, so it waits as a named operator step («Live round on the trimmed product»'s).

row.path: message: the operator, relaying the driving overseer as delegate
row.why: Q1 answered option 1, keep every v at 1: a delegate answer, PROVISIONAL; the bump-rule exception escalated at the wrap for the founder own word; the five leans stand

body:
- (v2-04) matrix#v2-04 — An automated send is never refused on budget and no budget surface remains: the identifier
  probe `grep -rn -E 'BudgetGate|BudgetPaused|…|\bPercent\b' src crates tests schemas fuzz/fuzz_targets Cargo.toml
  .config` exits 1 with no output; `send`'s refusal order is pinned by literal without a budget rung; `viola release
  --budget` is refused by clap (`release_args_refuse_the_budget_flag`) and a channel `release` carrying any `budget`
  key is `-32602` with no wheel moved (`release_carrying_a_budget_key_is_invalid_params_and_moves_no_wheel`, its
  control `holds`); the `list` payload is `{items, skipped}`; the ledger relies on 23 rows and none is
  `statusline-rate-limits` (`contract_ledger_probes`); no refusal maps to exit 11
  (`exit_codes_of_the_refusals_leave_eleven_unused`); the config keys and the log schema hold no budget key (the
  second probe). (per `architecture · decision/budget-governor-soft-stop` retired; census F-08)

- (compat) A new reader reads a 0.1.0-shaped snapshot and log: `snapshot_of_a_budget_era_writer_reads_whole_skipping_its_budget_fields`,
  `replay_over_a_budget_era_log_skips_its_gate_lines`; a written snapshot names no budget key
  (`snapshot_written_holds_no_budget_key`). The old-reader direction is measured, not run: a 0.1.0 reader fails to
  parse a new snapshot and reads the instance unreachable (research.md «Measured facts»; `inputs#I3`). (per
  `architecture · decision/versioned-tolerant-own-formats`)

- (ledger) A stamp holding the retired row reads on the relied rows alone
  (`verified_reads_a_stamp_holding_the_retired_row_on_the_relied_rows_alone`). (per `architecture ·
  decision/version-verified-all-relied-rows`)

- (driver guard) A `release` carrying a string `from` is still refused `-32602` `release-from-driver` first, its line
  unchanged (the existing wheel cases and `tests/cli_wheel.rs`). (per `architecture ·
  contract/channel-release/release-from-driver`)

- (board) The BAY line reads `BAY  skipped a - b - c`, the WHEEL column 23, and no non-budget row's bytes move
  (`tests/cli_list.rs` literals, `src/human/board` units). (per `layout-templates · contract/viola-list-board/column-widths`)

- (start) A start writes `wheel{cause:"start"}` then the hook's `session-start`, and boot readiness reads those two
  (`tests/path1_run_start.rs`, the smoke boot). (per `test-plan · contract/viola-run-start/event-order` less
  `budget-gate`)
- (tests) every gate of the block green; the control `release-budget` reads `holds`.

- Rows: `architecture · decision/budget-governor-soft-stop`, `decision/protocol-version-bump-rule`,
  `decision/run-start-order`, `contract/send-refusal/order`, `contract/channel-methods/release`,
  `contract/channel-release/release-from-driver`, `contract/list-payload/ok`, `contract/instance-snapshot/data`,
  `decision/snapshot-replay-log-fields-only`, `decision/versioned-tolerant-own-formats`,
  `decision/config-keys-match-schema`, `contract/config-json/unknown-keys`; `security-plan ·
  decision/release-from-driver-guard`, `decision/budget-gate-fails-open`, `decision/bounded-readers-census`;
  `design-system · contract/cli-exit-codes/11`, `decision/wheel-column-width-23`; `layout-templates ·
  contract/bay-line/cell-order`, `contract/viola-list-board/column-widths`; `test-plan ·
  decision/send-refusal-order`, `contract/boot-readiness/events`, `decision/product-state-never-hand-written`;
  `obs-plan · decision/unemittable-schema-words-removed`, `contract/config-json/known-keys`; `a11y-plan ·
  decision/one-hint-per-code`, `decision/no-hint-names-release`.
- Research files inspected: research.md «Files inspected» (`doc:2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed/research`).
- External: `inputs#I1` (the directive), `inputs#I3` (Q1's answer, a delegate's, PROVISIONAL).

- A `v` bump (snapshot, channel `params`, event line) — rejected on Q1's answer (`inputs#I3`, PROVISIONAL): an old
  reader fails closed either way; a bump written into files cannot be taken back without a second break.

- A compat shim writing `budget_paused:false` into new snapshots for old readers — rejected: v2-04 says no paused
  state remains.

- Skipping a `budget` key on `release` as an unknown field — rejected: an old `release --budget` meant «leave the
  wheel», and a skipped key hands a human-held wheel to the driver; it would also admit an input the wrapper refuses
  today (the playbook's «Boundary widening» pattern, `rul-r74hshif`).
- Narrowing WHEEL to 7 — rejected: every row's bytes and the 65-column NAME cap would move on a founder-ratified board.

- Re-recording `Mcp.tools-list-1.json` — not this chunk's: it needs a live `claude` start (`inputs#I1` item 3); its
  replay reads no description.
- Renumbering any exit code into 11, or giving 11 to another refusal — never.
- `#[ignore]` or a skip for a removed budget test — never: deleted (a11y · decision/zero-flakiness).

- Leaned the ledger row out HERE per v2-04's requirement («no `statusline-rate-limits` ledger row») and census C-205,
  C-286, C-587, C-747; the next entry's «21 relied rows» is 24 − 1 here − 2 there.

- Leaned the `budget`-key refusal per CLAUDE.md «The human always wins» and `rul-r74hshif`; leaned WHEEL 23 per the
  layouts history (founder's confirmation 2026-10-13, board width 2026-10-20); the five leans stand on `inputs#I3`.

- The test the relay asks for in the other direction (an old reader over a new snapshot) has no 0.1.0 reader in the
  tree: it is stated as measured, never claimed as run.

- If the founder's word changes Q1 to a bump before implement ends, the revision adds: `SNAPSHOT_V` 2 with a reader
  accepting 1 and 2 and its `state-recovered{snapshot-unsupported-v}` cases; `PROTOCOL_V` 2 on the client and the
  wrapper with the `-32602` `unsupported-version` cases both ways; the `list` document's `v`; the harness's readers of
  each; and the masters' contract rows for each `v`.

- Counts by rule: `EventKind::ALL` 16 → 15 (`crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs:78`); relied 24 → 23
  (`LedgerRow::relied()`); `CONFIG_KEYS` 6 → 4 (`src/obs.rs:33`); the ci kill filter loses one `binary(…)`
  (`.config/nextest.toml:24`); the root `WITHIN` waits move with `tests/cli_budget.rs` — each re-measured by its rule at
  the wrap.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Conventions — `decision/protocol-version-bump-rule` gains an exception
  naming this retirement, PROVISIONAL (a delegate's answer, `inputs#I3`), escalated on the wrap's card for the
  founder's own word.

- Expected amendments (wrap): the census F-08 rows (213, each `→ v2-04`, `doc:viola-0.2.0/census`) retire across the
  seven masters and the harness files (`D-retired`): the budget decisions and contracts of architecture,
  security-plan, design-system, layout-templates, test-plan, obs-plan and a11y-plan named in the rows files.

- Expected amendments (wrap): design-system §Surface: cli — `decision/wheel-column-width-23`'s reason re-worded (the
  width kept; its widest word gone).

- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan §6 — `decision/snapshot-replay-from-log`'s guard re-pointed off `cli_budget`
  (to `a_start_over_an_unreadable_snapshot_replays_the_log` and the `cli_links` case).

## 2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed — Conventions: 7 row(s) (1 of 2)
**Section:** Conventions
**Change:** + decision/retired-exit-codes-never-reused — Retired exit codes never reused
~ decision/json-field-names-snake-case · except: was «`last_assistant_message`, `resets_at` and `used_percentage` stay as Claude emits them.»; now «`last_assistant_message` stays as Claude emits it.»
~ decision/protocol-version-bump-rule · except: was «»; now «Removing the budget gate's fields and event kind kept every own-format `v` at 1 (snapshot, channel params, event line, list document); readers skip the removed keys and kind.»
~ decision/unparseable-external-values-unknown · rule: was «An unparseable external value becomes the string `"unknown"` in viola's own records, never an error, covering `resets_at`, `used_percentage` and a missing statusline window.»; now «An unparseable external value becomes the string `"unknown"` in viola's own records, never an error.»
~ contract/cli-exit-codes/11 · promise: was «The `budget-paused` refusal.»; now «Unassigned: the retired `budget-paused` refusal's code, never reused or renumbered.»
~ contract/cli-verbs/release · promise: was «`viola release <target> [--budget]`.»; now «`viola release <target>`; a `--budget` flag is a usage error (exit 2).»

**Why:** decision/retired-exit-codes-never-reused: Exit 11 left with budget-paused and was retired, never renumbered or reused, which binds every later exit-code assignment.
decision/json-field-names-snake-case: The rate-limits reading and its resets_at and used_percentage fields are gone from every viola format.
decision/protocol-version-bump-rule: The founder ruled that every own-format v stays 1 for this removal, written as an exception to the bump rule. — resolved by the operator (Q1): relayed verbatim by overseer1, 2026-11-14, inputs#I8: «Подтвердить (Recommended)»
decision/unparseable-external-values-unknown: resets_at, used_percentage and the statusline window are no longer read, so the row no longer covers them.
contract/cli-exit-codes/11: budget-paused is gone and nothing maps to exit 11, which stays retired and is never reused.
contract/cli-verbs/release: release's --budget flag was removed and clap now refuses it with exit 2.
contract/mcp-tool-results/success: The list ok payload lost its budget member.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-14T16-46-26-wrap/

~ decision/snapshot-replay-log-fields-only · rule: was «A snapshot rebuilt by replay recovers only links, agent_session_id, wheel and the budget gate from the log; a field no line gave is absent, never a default.»; now «A snapshot rebuilt by replay recovers only links, agent_session_id and wheel from the log; a field no line gave is absent, never a default.»
~ decision/statusline-hook-exempt · rule: was «`viola hook statusline` records the `rate_limits` reading, prints the user's statusline command's stdout unchanged, and always exits 0 with empty stderr.»; now «`viola hook statusline` prints the user's statusline command's stdout unchanged and always exits 0 with empty stderr.»
~ contract/channel-methods/release-type-check · promise: was «A `release` whose `from` is of a non-string type, or whose `budget` is not a bool (`null` included), is `-32602` with `data: null`; this check comes first.»; now «A `release` whose `from` is of a non-string type, or that carries a `budget` key of any value (`null` included), is `-32602` `invalid-params` with `data: null`, no wheel moved and no record; only the string-`from` refusal comes before it.»

**Why:** decision/list-reads-state-directly: list no longer reads a budget file or thresholds.

decision/statusline-hook-exempt: The statusline wrapper no longer reads or records rate_limits.

body:
# Wrap of 2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed — the cascade's listing: the ruling (the pipeline's owner, relayed)

The 2.3 MB listing (`sweep-pass-1.*`, 47 parts) is NOT read. Its volume is one defect of the tool's pattern writer: a
bare number taken as a «distinctive term» and joined as a substring alternative. Measured in this run dir: 13 patterns
carry ≈ 15 000 of the 18 312 rows — arch1-62 `budget\.json|1` (2165) · arch1-1 `0|100` · arch1-63 · arch1-64 ·
security1-13 · -15 · -16 · obs1-19 · -20 · layouts1-7 · layouts1-8 `0` · tests1-57 (≈ 1200 each) · tests1-8 `3` (505);
then `11` in obs1-27 · tests1-32 · tests1-45 · tests1-53 (≈ 200 each). The files cannot be regenerated (the landing
moved the ground the dry run read), so this wrap takes the mend by hand, as the tool will write it once mended:

1. In each `cascade-patterns-{doc}-{k}.toml` (the nine; main's own `cascade-patterns.toml` untouched) remove every
   term that is a NUMBER ALONE (digits, with an inner `.` or `,`: 0 · 1 · 3 · 11 · 62 · 85 · 89 · 90 · 100 · 3339 ·
   32603 · 89.6 …). A term holding a letter stays (5H · 7D · 4m · 25th; 10-14 and 10/11/12/14 stay — they are not
   numbers alone). A pattern left with ONE term becomes `fixed`, as the tool spells it; a pattern left with NO term is
   removed whole. By a short script, never by hand line by line; first keep a byte copy of the nine files as written
   beside them (`.raw-` twins).
2. Run `cascade.py sweep` again, the same call. The NEW pass is the listing step 2 reads whole and dispositions;
   pass 1's 47 parts are not read.
3. `cascade-dispositions.md` names, in its search section: the mend (bare-number terms dropped from the tool's files,
   on this ruling), each pattern removed whole with its row handle, and that those rows' changed numbers were NOT
   swept — step 3's leaves read each such row's delta, the letter's own arm for a change that yields no term.
4. If the new listing is still past what one window reads (over ≈ 400 KB), STOP again and print its `total` and
   `per class` lines and the ten heaviest patterns — do not read by parts across windows.

What this stops catching: a leaf line that repeats a retired NUMBER and none of the row's names (a threshold «90», an
exit «11»). Main's own patterns already carry the exit-11 and threshold phrasings, and the leaves step reads the
deltas.

Then the wrap goes on as the skill says: the leaves step and its batch, P2's friction record, P3–P7, the one-block
report of the wrap directive (`inputs#I7`) at the end. After the commit and push start nothing more.

row.why: the pipeline owner's ruling on the cascade's 2.3 MB listing: bare-number terms dropped from the tool-written pattern files (raw twins kept), the sweep re-run, pass 1 not read; stop again past 400 KB

body: - The budget gate on automated sends is removed whole (its thresholds, the `budget-paused` refusal, `release --budget` and its Path 6 guards); exit 11 is retired (was `budget-paused`) and never reused, and an older wrapper's `budget-paused` refusal reads as unknown, exit 14.

- On the CLI, state is always a printed word (`stale`, `DIALOG <kind>`, `expired`, `unverified-cli`, the STATUS words `idle` / `busy` on joined wrapped rows and the unwrapped rows' `n/a` cells; on a terminal too narrow only an unwrapped NAME is cut, to the column less 3 characters plus `...` and never inside a `\xHH` escape, a wrapped NAME never, and piped output and `--json` keep every name whole); colour is a second cue only (amber SGR only on `DIALOG`, dim on stale rows, bold only on NAME values, always beside the word), `unable` / `fail` are never coloured, and viola emits no SGR of its own under non-TTY / `NO_COLOR` (an empty value included) / `TERM=dumb` / `--json` / `viola run` / a passed `viola revive`, and `viola link` / `viola unlink` print one plain-ASCII result line in one write with no SGR in any mode. viola has no web or graphical frontend, so no page token pair or layout to verify.
- `src/cmd/<subcommand>.rs` — one module per subcommand; `src/run/` — PTY pump, wheel, readiness-gate wiring.
- Unparseable external values become `"unknown"`, never an error, except a hyprctl reply the Hyprland seam cannot parse, which is the seam's `malformed` error.
- JSON field names snake_case (Claude's own `last_assistant_message` kept); enum values kebab-case (`#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]`).

- CLI exit codes: 0 · 1 (a `cli` verb's internal error: `error: internal error` on stderr, or under `--json` before a `--` the catch site's `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout, stderr then empty, `run`, `revive`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` silent at that site; also `viola run`'s and `viola revive`'s start, and `viola verify`, refusing the home tree before any log opens: the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or the instance-state pair for an instance-level refusal, no line written, no child started; also `viola run` and `viola revive`'s start refusing the socket directory (`socket_dir_ready`, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`; a failed create and a refused check read this one code, a `Server::bind` failure does not): the stderr `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or under `viola revive --json` the `socket-dir-refused` document, and one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"socket-dir-refused"}`, no path, pid or uid; `viola verify`'s refusals each carry their code on the `process-exit` it writes under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`: `program-not-found` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `version-unreadable` · `strict-modes-failed` · `unclean-fixture`, beside `interrupted`; a failing row is no refusal and carries no code, yet `viola verify` still exits 1 on a failed relied row with that row's stamp written, and `verify` takes no `--json`) · 2 (usage error, and `viola send` text over 16 MiB or not UTF-8) · 10 human-typing · 11 unassigned (the retired `budget-paused` refusal's code, never reused or renumbered) · 12 unverified-cli · 13 not-delivered · 14 unknown · 20 wrapper fault (a `-32602` from `link` / `unlink` included) · 21 instance unreachable (under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, written by `client::unreachable_document` (the board builds its own), `<cause>` one of `viola_core::UnreachableCause`'s closed words `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`, no `RefusalReason`; with no live endpoint `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint` reads an instance directory as `instance-dead` and anything else as `unwrapped-name`, so a stale instance reads `instance-dead`, and a wrapper lost with the call open reads `endpoint-lost`; also, on `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink`, a server that is not the recorded wrapper — a connected peer whose euid is not this user's or cannot be read (`peer_admitted`), or the connected peer's pid or OS start time not the snapshot's, or that check not made — no frame written, `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"server-verify-failed"}` under `--json` (Linux only; the Windows and macOS legs left with their code, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`), after the client's own exit-13 refusals, the strict-modes instance check and the socket-directory check, with no exit code or `RefusalReason` of its own, its `--json` word the document's `detail`; also `viola list`'s refused strict-modes check of the home, `instances/` or any one instance, which refuses the whole board, no log opened; and `viola plugin install`'s refused strict-modes check of the home or an existing `marketplace/` tree dir, nothing created, no log opened; and the refused instance check of `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` (the target instance) and of `viola link` / `viola unlink` (the driven instance), made first by `client::refuse_untrusted` (`check_instance` on the home and `instances/<name>`, after `send`'s text read, before any connect, role file or log opens): the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` under `--json`, no log opened, no line written; and, on those same eight verbs, past that check and before any connect, a refused socket directory on the recorded endpoint (`check_endpoint_dir` in `client::connect`): the socket-directory hint last on stderr, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"socket-dir-refused"}` under `--json`, one `process-exit` at WARN with `during` `connect` and no `channel-request`); `viola hook` always 0. `viola revive` exits 0, 1 for a refused strict-modes check (ahead of the wrapper log: the stderr pair, no log line) or a preflight refusal (`already-live` or `stale-heartbeat` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing`, read in that order, each one `process-exit` line) or a refusal of the start after a passed preflight, or 2 for a usage error; it takes `--json` on both arms, where a refused strict-modes check and every refusal of its start is instead one stdout document `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`, by `client::refused_document`; a `claude` not on `PATH` or an anyhow error of the start is `internal-error`), stderr empty, exit 1, and `<name> --list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}` in log order (a `pump_child` error prints no document: the child has held the terminal).
- Flags kebab-case long options (`--json`, `--file`, global `--home`); subcommands single lower-case words (`plugin install` the one two-word verb).

- Arguments mirror channel params: `viola send <target>` (text from stdin or `--file`), `viola wait <target> [--after <cursor>] [--timeout-ms <n>]`, `viola last <target>`, `viola answer <target> <dialog_id>` (response JSON from stdin/`--file`), `viola pause <target>`, `viola release <target>` (a `--budget` flag is a usage error, exit 2), `viola link|unlink <driver> <driven>`; `viola revive <name> [--id <ID>] [--fork] [-- <child args>]` and `viola revive <name> --list` send no channel frame.

- `config.json` is parsed tolerantly (unknown keys skipped and counted) and carries `v`; keys: `diagnostics_level` (`info` by default, or `debug`; the only source of the process-log level, `RUST_LOG` having no effect; obs D-15), `claude_env_keep` (the R8 pass-list of `CLAUDE*` names, an array of at most 32 names each matching `^CLAUDE[A-Z0-9_]*$`, default empty; a bad value is rejected whole, and an identity-floor name in it has no effect), `dialog_hold_s` (the dialog hold as a `DialogHold`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, read once at the wrapper's start; any other value takes 60 with one `parse-rejected` line, so no value makes the hold zero or unbounded).

- Crate dependency direction is enforced by manifests: `viola-core` depends on no viola crate; `viola-pty` knows no agent; `viola-hyprland` is the one compositor seam (queries and dispatches only through its closed request set), sync and tokio-free, depending on `viola-core` alone among viola crates; only `viola-agent-claude` knows Claude payload shapes; among the product crates only `viola-mcp` enables tokio (`rt`), and `viola-channel` lists it optional behind its `tokio` feature (the `TokioClient`), which `viola-mcp` enables; the root bin holds the subcommand dispatch, the run pump and the wheel, all of which consume only normalised events.

The only crate that knows Claude Code. It parses hook payloads tolerantly and maps each hook to a normalised kind. It maps dialog answers to decision bodies (S3 / S7 / S8) and applies the R8 `CLAUDE*` strip. It resolves the child program (`resolve_program`: a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`) and holds the Claude-specific half of the CLI version gate: the capability ledger rows (compiled) with their `viola verify` checks, `parse_version`, the stamp merge and `verified` verdict, and the fixture scrub. The gate's spawn is the root bin's `run::version_gate`; the stamps I/O is `viola_state::stamps`. It keeps the vt100 screen signatures (readiness gate), parses, in the pure `agents` module, a `claude agents --json` answer (`parse` into rows or a closed `AgentsFailure`, `oversize` · `malformed`; the read itself is the root bin's `run::agents`), and normalises `prompt-submitted` (removes the long-paste wrapper, then reverses tag escaping; classifies `origin` driver/human/harness). It also holds the resume shapes `viola revive` launches with (`viola verify`'s Run E is the second caller of `resume_args(id, false)`): `PROGRAM` (`claude`), `RESUME_FLAG`, `FORK_SESSION_FLAG`, `is_session_id` (36 characters, hyphens at offsets 8, 13, 18, 23, ASCII hex elsewhere) and `resume_args(id, fork)`; it is the one product home of the two flag literals. It also holds the pure `marketplace` module, `viola plugin install`'s three documents built by `serde_json` (`marketplace_files`; `NAME` the marketplace `viola`, `PLUGIN_REF` `viola@viola`; its `.mcp.json` registers the MCP server `viola`, no hooks). No adapter trait yet: a second agent arrives as a sibling `viola-agent-<name>` crate, at which point the adapter trait is extracted into `viola-core`.

- The pure `statusline` module (as landed; chrono for it, no file, clock or environment read): `user_command` (a `statusLine` of type `command`, non-empty, no NUL), `override_document` and `shell_argv` (`/bin/sh -c`, `shell_argv` the fixed three-element argv `[&str; 3]`), `SETTINGS_FLAG`, `USER_SETTINGS`, `BIN_SH`, `SHELL_FLAG` and `probe_document` (the document behind Run B's probe `--settings`, `typed/statusline.json`). Its two CLI shapes are the ledger rows `statusline-override` · `statusline-shell` (since chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows), relied on every build (`LedgerRow::relied()` holds all twenty-three rows; architecture, Capability ledger).

- Ledger rows (S3, S7, S8, R8 identity floor, shim resolution, the settings-override mechanism and the shell (rows `statusline-override` · `statusline-shell` since chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, relied on every build), harness prefixes, `<pasted_content>` wrapper, modal / input-box signatures, hook tier map, turn end without Stop, dialog concurrency, `claude agents --json` join field (row `agents-join` since chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board: both `pid` and `sessionId` exposed, relied on every build), local commands + post-conditions, tag escaping, largest hook payload) are compiled here, never built from runtime or upstream text.

- `ledger` module (as landed, pure, no I/O): `LedgerRow`, twenty-three closed rows (the members of `LedgerRow::ALL`, in its order) `shim-resolution` · `spine-hooks` · `session-start-fields` · `prompt-verbatim` · `stop-message` · `largest-hook-payload` · `modal-signature` · `input-box-signature` · `quiet-period` · `confirm-window` · `question-answer` · `plan-approve-revise` · `question-notes` · `dialog-concurrency` · `long-paste-wrapper` · `tag-escaping` · `local-command-clear` · `paste-newline` · `statusline-override` · `statusline-shell` · `resume-session` · `agents-join` · `local-command-compact`; the relied set `LedgerRow::relied()` (every row of `ALL`, in its order, all twenty-three); `ShellVerdict`, `StatusLineCapture`, `statusline_variants` (`StatusLine.default-1.json`, `StatusLine.rate-limits-1.json`) and the `StatusLine.<k>` file-name helpers; `resume_target` (Run E's target id: the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture, only when `is_session_id` accepts it) and `resume_variants` (`SessionStart.resume-1.json`); `AgentsCapture` / `agents_variant` (Run B's agents capture and its `Agents.recorded-1.json` filter); `TypedRun`, `Probes { print, typed, trusted, dialogs, statusline, resumed, agents }` (`trusted`: Run B's captures in claim order; `statusline`: Run B's status line captures in `k` order; `resumed`: Run E's captures in claim order; `agents`: Run B's one agents capture, an `AgentsCapture`, on which `agents-join` passes only when it parses and holds exactly one row whose `pid` is Run B's child pid, whose `sessionId` is the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture and whose status is idle or busy (`agents_joined`), and fails with no capture; the `local-command-compact` row passes only when the first SessionStart capture of source `compact` after the newline turn's prompt (`compact_start`) has a non-empty `session_id` equal to that of Run B's first SessionStart capture, no UserPromptSubmit carries `/compact`, and `compact_latency_ms` is within `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (`local_command_compacted`)); Run B's six compiled paste texts (`PROBE_PROMPT`, `PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE` (113 bytes, ASCII, exactly one LF at neither end, no CR) and `PROBE_COMPACT_COMMAND` (the list's `/compact`) among them); `FRAMING_TURNS` (in paste order `paste-1` · `paste-2` · `paste-3` · `compact-1` · `clear-1`) and `framing_stem`; `CAPTURE_EVENTS`; `parse_version` (first line exactly `X.Y.Z (Claude Code)`); `capture_plugin_files` (plugin `viola-verify-probe`, four exec-form `--capture` hooks); `check(row, &Probes)`, `largest`; `merge_stamp` (writes `measured.typed_probe`), `verified` (every row of `LedgerRow::relied()` `pass`, all twenty-three on every build, a stamp holding a retired ledger row verifying on the relied rows alone; a stamp holding exactly the seventeen ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row holds, or exactly the eighteen ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows holds, or exactly the twenty-one ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows holds, or exactly the twenty-two ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board holds, or exactly the twenty-three ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row holds, all `pass`, reads unverified; so every home stamped before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row reads `cli_verified:false` until its next `viola verify`); `scrub`, `is_clean` (reads through `unclean`), `signature_rows`, `screen_is_clean`, `screen_fault` → `ScreenFault { row, seam, why }`, `unclean` → the closed `Unclean` codes `home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email`. `verified` returns `Result<bool, AgentError>`: a wrong-shaped envelope is `AgentError::StampsMalformed` ("the capability stamps are malformed"). `AgentError` sits at the crate root and also holds `resolve_program`'s one refusal, `ProgramNotFound`, with a fixed message (arch [Error Handling]). `resolve_program` returns `Result<PathBuf, AgentError>`, in the crate and in the root wrapper `src/run/mod.rs`.

The shared vocabulary of every other crate: the normalised event kinds, `RefusalReason` and its closed detail sets (`HumanTyping { ManualPause }` among them), `UnreachableCause` (`StrictModes` · `InstanceDead` · `UnwrappedName` · `EndpointLost` · `ServerVerify` · `SocketDir`, each word through `as_str`, `SocketDir`'s `socket-dir-refused`: exit 21's closed cause set, with no serde path, the two clients writing every word, and no `RefusalReason`), the wheel's `WheelCause` (`start` · `human-input` · `manual-pause` · `release`), the nutype newtypes `ViolaName` and `DialogHold` (whole seconds 60–3600), the protocol `v` constants, the shared validators (`validate_paste_text`, and `is_code_word`: 1 to 64 bytes of `[a-z0-9-]`, a lower-case letter first), the `MAX_FRAME` constant (16 MiB), `SPINE_DEADLINE` (1 s, the spine bound the perf gate reads), `DIALOG_HOLD_DEFAULT` · `DIALOG_HOLD_MIN` · `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX` (60 s · 60 s · 3600 s, PROVISIONAL: the dialog hold's default and bounds, `config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s` read once at the wrapper's start into a `DialogHold`; the hook bounds its reply read at `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s`, below the `hooks.json` `timeout` of 3615), the injected `Clock` seam (`SystemClock` in production; first consumer `run`'s vt100 feed thread), `SERVICE_NAME` / `VERSION`, and the obs vocabulary (`obs_event!`, `ObsEvent`, `ObsProcess`). It performs no I/O and depends on no viola crate. It does NOT know Claude payload shapes (that is `viola-agent-claude`), and it does not depend on `tracing`: `obs_event!` expands to `::tracing::event!` at the caller.
Nothing inside the workspace. Third-party: nutype 0.8.0 (`ViolaName`, `DialogHold`) and serde (`derive`), with the dev-dependency serde_json (via `[workspace.dependencies]`).

- New event kinds and refusal details are added ONLY here, never with Claude-specific names; `detail` values are kebab-case strings from a closed set per reason (`unknown`'s a code word or null). `EventKind` holds 15 kinds (the length of `EventKind::ALL`; `budget-gate` is no longer one), the dialog kinds `question` / `permission` / `plan` among them, `link` / `unlink` (`data` keys `driver`, `driven`) and, last, `dialog-expired` (`data` keys `dialog_id`, `dialog_kind`; `source: wrapper`, appended once when a held dialog's hold ends); `EventKind::WAIT_WAKE` is the one wake set (`turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end`, `dialog-expired`) the wrapper's `wait` and the channel's `outcome` both read.
- No usage-budget gate: no subscription rate-limit reading and no budget state, so this crate holds no budget reading, window word, threshold or `budget-paused` refusal.

Everything on disk: viola home resolution (`--home` → grandparent of `VIOLA_DIR` → `~/.viola/`; as landed (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract) `hook` and every CLI verb, `run` and `revive` included, take the `VIOLA_DIR` step through the root bin's `resolve_home` / `resolved_home` (`src/cmd/mod.rs`), only when `VIOLA_NAME` and `VIOLA_DIR` pass `instance_of`'s shape check, a failing pair falling through to the default, never refusing; `viola mcp` resolves its home through the same `resolved_home`), ndjson append logs (one `write` per line), atomic JSON snapshots (tempfile `persist` through the one helper `fs::replace_private` / `replace_private_shared`), std `File::lock` on `.lock` siblings (opened for write), the `events.ndjson` reader `events::read_from` (each line under `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` with its start and end offsets; per-read counts `unknown_kinds` · `unknown_fields` · `torn_lines`; a line of an unknown kind is not returned; an over-long line, a non-object line and the unterminated last line count as torn, the last neither returned nor rewritten), the healing append (an append to a log whose last byte is not LF writes one LF and its line in one write, then logs `state-recovered`), liveness (heartbeat + sysinfo pid/start time; `liveness::start_times`, one process-table read; `liveness::live_endpoint(instance_dir)` → `Option<LiveEndpoint>` (`{ endpoint, pid, started_at }`, all from its one `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` call and only on a real snapshot: a replayed or absent one, or a failed read, gives `None`), shared by CLI `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink` and `viola-mcp`'s frame tools, and giving none for a stale wrapper too; `liveness::without_endpoint(instance_dir)` → `UnreachableCause`, where `live_endpoint` gives none: read through `symlink_metadata`, a directory is `InstanceDead`, anything else (absent, a regular file, a symlink) `UnwrappedName`, opening nothing and writing no line, behind the strict-modes check at both callers, `client::Unreachable::without_endpoint` and `viola-mcp`'s `frame`; the server identity check (the closed `ServerVerdict` `Matches` · `Mismatch` · `Unverifiable`, the pure `server_verdict`, the joined `verify_server` reading the observed start time through `process_start_time`: the snapshot's pid and start time against the connected server's, made before the first frame by those CLI verbs, `viola hook` and `viola-mcp`'s frame tools; with no peer pid reported, `Unverifiable`, no frame written)), the classified snapshot read (`snapshot::read_snapshot_classified`) and the log replay (`replay`: library code, read through `read_snapshot_or_replay` by six product readers, each after the instance's strict-modes check: `viola revive`'s preflight (one read for both its collision check and its recorded directory), `viola list`'s `board::read`, `liveness::live_endpoint`, `viola hook`'s `connect`, `hook statusline`'s `serve` and `run`'s collision check; no product code under `src/` calls `read_snapshot`; `replay::session_chain` gives one link per `session-start` line with a string id, with the pass's skip counts, and writes and logs nothing), the optional snapshot field `cwd` (the start's spawn directory; no event carries it, so a replay gives none), the instance check `strict::check_instance` (the home (the read rule), `instances/` (the write rule), the instance directory (the read rule), its `diagnostics/` (the read rule), its `snapshot.json` (the write rule) and its `events.ndjson` (the write rule), each that exists, a folder before what it holds), `ledger/stamps.json` reads (`config.json` is read by the root bin, `run::dialog::read_hold`, not here), and the home strict-modes check (Unix owner + modes) with 0700/0600 creation, in two rules — the write rule, and the read rule (`unix_read_verdict`: no group or other bit) —, and beside `check_instance` the checks `check_home_tree(home, name, key)` (the home; with a name `check_instance`'s set; `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`; with a key `bin/<key>/`, the pinned `viola`, `plugin/<key>/`, its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/`; each that exists; refusing as `TreeRefused::HomeLevel` or `TreeRefused::InstanceLevel`; called by `run`'s and `revive`'s starts and by `verify` with no name and no key), `check_diagnostics` (a symbolic link refused; run by `open_role_file` / `write_detail` before anything is narrowed), `check_stamps` and `check_socket_dir` (one `symlink_metadata`: an absent path passes, an unstattable one is `Refused::Unreadable`, then `socket_dir_verdict` reads a symlink as `Refused::Symlink`, a non-directory as the fixed-message `Refused::NotADirectory` and anything else by the read rule; it never chmods, a refused directory stays as found), with `check_endpoint_dir`, that check on a recorded endpoint's parent, run before a bind (`viola run`, `revive`'s start) and before each client's connect (the CLI frame verbs, `hook`, `viola-mcp`'s `frame`).

- Only the instance's wrapper writes its snapshot; only `viola verify` writes stamps; no process writes or reads a `budget.json` (no budget reading is kept). The board read model is `board.rs` (`scan` checks the home by the read rule (`check_read`, on Linux, with or without an instance, a refusal `ScanRefused::Home`), `instances/` by `check_path` and each instance without following a link; `read` gives one `Item` per live or stale instance, takes the replay for an unreadable or newer snapshot, and sums the skip counts of one `read_from` pass per instance; the agents join (`JoinKeys`, `Observation`, `join`, `Item::unwrapped`) folds one `claude agents --json` reading in: a row matching a wrapped item's `child_pid` or `agent_session_id` sets that item's `status` to `idle` or `busy`, and every unjoined row is an unwrapped item; no type holds `endpoint`, `pinned_bin`, `cwd`, `statusline_command`, `pid`, `started_at` or `links`). The snapshot holds no budget field (`budget_paused` and `budget_override_until` are gone; `v` stays 1). The snapshot holds an optional `statusline_command`; `SnapshotRead::Present` and `replay::Recovered::Snapshot` hold a `Box<InstanceSnapshot>`.

- **Crate-level:** `crates/viola-state/tests/state_events.rs` (the 15 kinds round-trip, the three counts, the heal) and `state_replay.rs` (the classified read and the replay, the two link cases, the snapshot left untouched)

The `viola` binary. It holds the clap 4.6.7 dispatch (`src/main.rs`, one module per subcommand in `src/cmd/`) and the `run` wrapper (`src/run/`): the PTY pump, the wheel, the readiness-gate wiring and the channel server dispatch. **"Strip-bay handoff, read back."** The direction the CLI carries, and the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) inherits, is an air-traffic-control tower strip bay after dark. Buff paper strips sit in anthracite holder boots on ruled aluminium racks, and every session keeps its slot for life. The only warm light is the one amber arrival holder cocked out of line when a session needs you. The voice is standard phraseology: short fixed words (`open`, `RB`, `unable`, `human-typing`, `not-delivered`), no filler, no guessing. Nothing announces success before it is confirmed: a send stays `open` until the matching `prompt-submitted` reads it back (on a verified CLI, for `/clear` until its new-session post-condition does and for `/compact` until its same-session compact post-condition does; on an unverified CLI both `/clear` and `/compact` stay `unconfirmable`). Missing readings print `unknown`. It is explicitly NOT a monitoring dashboard: no status dots, toasts, graphs, spinners or glow.
